name: Lane Spring Recreation Area
note: USFS Mark Twain NF campground on Little Piney Creek (trout stream) near Rolla; 17 sites (6 electric, 11 basic) with 6 creekside, RVs to ~34 ft; sites are FCFS (only the group pavilion is reservable); open Apr-Oct. --Claude

name: Paddy Creek Recreation Area
note: USFS Mark Twain NF campground nestled along Paddy Creek near Licking; 19 non-electric sites (asphalt pads to ~34 ft), no potable water; FCFS via fee tube; open Apr-Dec. --Claude

name: Marble Creek Recreation Area
note: USFS Mark Twain NF campground on Marble Creek near Fredericktown (Ozark Trail trailhead); 26 non-electric sites, 6 directly creekside, no potable water; FCFS via fee tube; open Apr-Oct. --Claude

name: Float Camp Recreation Area
note: USFS Mark Twain NF campground ~150 ft from the Current River near Doniphan; some 30/50A electric and many non-electric sites (RVs to 40 ft) with pressurized water; individual sites are FCFS; open ~Apr-Oct. --Claude

name: Markham Springs Recreation Area
note: USFS Mark Twain NF campground on the Black River near Ellsinore; a 50A electric loop (Birch) plus three non-electric loops, with showers and drinking water; reservable online May-Labor Day, FCFS otherwise; open May-Oct. --Claude

name: Cobb Ridge Recreation Area
note: Developed USFS Mark Twain NF campground for the Chadwick motorized-trail area near Chadwick; 45 sites incl. ~25 electric (30/50A), paved pads to 45 ft with showers; standard sites reservable online plus some FCFS; open year-round (no horses). --Claude

name: Powder Mill Campground
note: Primitive FCFS NPS Ozark Riverways campground (~8-10 sites) on the Current River ~12 mi east of Eminence; no electric, RVs/trailers to 35 ft, vault toilet and boat ramp; seasonal. --Claude  Since 2025 Ozark Riverways lists Powder Mill as a backcountry campground: reservations required on Recreation.gov (NPS backcountry campgrounds page, 2026-10-10). --Claude

name: Hunnewell Lake Conservation Area
note: FCFS primitive lakeside camping at Hunnewell Lake (MDC) with drive-through sites, vault toilets and a dump station behind the ranger station; no hookups. --Claude

name: Whetstone Creek Conservation Area
note: FCFS primitive camping (MDC) in level gravel lots beside Big Lake near Williamsburg; drive-in off a maintained gravel road, vault toilets, no hookups. --Claude

name: Deer Ridge Conservation Area
note: FCFS primitive camping (MDC) at several drive-in campgrounds off gravel roads near Lewistown, including a Lake Campground on Deer Ridge Lake; privies, no hookups. --Claude

name: Lead Mine Conservation Area
note: FCFS camping (MDC) at a ~50-site gravel main campground (about 26 sites fit trailers) with a privy, near the Niangua River and Jakes Creek; drive-in, no hookups. --Claude

name: Brookfield South City Park
note: City of Brookfield park with ~10 FCFS pull-through sites (30/50A electric and water) and a dump station via on-site fee box; front sites are more level for a 23-ft rig. --Claude

name: Shelbina Lake Campground
note: City of Shelbina park on Shelbina Lake with ~90 FCFS electric sites (mostly 30/50A) paid at the golf pro shop or City Hall; open late Mar-Oct. --Claude

name: Mozingo Lake Recreation Park
note: City of Maryville park on the roughly 1,000-acre Mozingo Lake, with three RV campgrounds: South (95 sites, on a peninsula), North (20 concrete sites) and a riders' equestrian campground on the west shore. 40 South and North sites are reservable online for up to 14 days; the rest are first come, first served and may stay longer at staff discretion. The South campground and its shower house stay open all winter; the North and Equestrian close from November 1 to March 1. --Claude

name: Powell's Creekside Haven
note: 46-acre Kingsville campground with 21 RV sites (10 full-hookup, 20/30/50A) plus a creek and pond; reservable. --Claude Rechecked 2026-10-01: operator site says TEMPORARILY CLOSED FOR MAJOR RENOVATION; no reopening date. --Claude

name: Chase State Fishing Lake
note: 109-acre KDWP state fishing lake in the Flint Hills west of Cottonwood Falls; primitive camping, first come first served, on about a dozen gravel spurs along the north shore, eight or nine of which suit an RV (camper report, April 2026). Vault toilets, no hookups. --Claude

name: Historic Lake Scott State Park
note: Spring-fed 100-acre lake in a wooded canyon 11 miles north of Scott City, with El Cuartelejo pueblo ruins in the park. Lakeview loop's east-side sites are the ones by the water. Since 2026-07 KDWP has been partly draining the lake to clear a bacteria and algae problem, with a KDHE no-contact advisory from 2026-06-25 (KDWP alerts, read 2026-11-06). --Claude

Booking: min stay 3 nights on holidays (Memorial Day, Independence Day and Labor Day weekends (2027 rule))

name: Goodman State Fishing Lake
note: KDWP state fishing lake (40-acre lake, 225-acre wildlife area) 5 mi S and 2.5 mi E of Ness City. Primitive camping beside the gravel parking areas above the lake's west shore, with picnic shelters, a vault toilet, a boat ramp and a courtesy dock. Roads are dirt and rut when wet (1/2026 camper). FCFS, 7 nights at most. --Claude

name: Lake Afton Park (Sedgwick County)
note: Sedgwick County park, 720 acres around the 258-acre Lake Afton, W of Wichita. RV camping in several areas around the shore (Fisherman's Cove by the observatory, Shelter #5 on Fellowship Cove, Cottonwood Grove), with electric at many sites, water at 16, a dump station and restrooms (three open in winter). No generators. Permits at the park office or kiosk, no reservations; 14 days, then 5 days away, 56 days a year at most. Blue-green algae warnings in summer (call 316-660-1780). --Claude

name: Lake Parsons (Labette County)
note: City of Parsons lake NW of Parsons in Labette County, reached by about 2 mi of unpaved road: an improved campsite area of concrete-slab sites with electric and water on a wooded peninsula, with boat ramp and docks, playground, bath house and a summer camp host; free primitive camping where there is no pad. Permits from the City Clerk ($300 a year), no reservations, 12-day limit. --Claude

name: Sleeping Elephant Campground
note: Roosevelt NF (Canyon Lakes RD) campground beside Hwy 14 in Poudre Canyon, ~43 mi west of US 287, ~7,800 ft, in open ponderosa pine with a view of Sleeping Elephant Mountain. The Cache la Poudre River runs across the highway, mostly through private land here. Length conflict (2026-10-28): the campground page gives parking lengths of 15-30 ft and says this older facility will not take larger RVs, but the forest's campground-status table lists a 20-ft maximum spur. --Claude Online photos show at least a few sites that can take a class-B or small class-C, but reviews say the sites are short and unlevel: have a backup plan. --AWH 2026-10-28

name: Little Maud Campground
note: White River NF campground at ~7,800 ft on the slope above the north end of Ruedi Reservoir, off Frying Pan Road (CR 104) about 16 mi east of Basalt, sharing the Ruedi complex entrance with Little Mattie and Mollie B; boat ramp and picnic ground below, walk down to the water. --Claude FS, read 2026-10-28: 'Due to lack of water the campground is now closed for the 2026 season.' --Claude 2026-10-28

name: Mollie B Campground
note: Aspen-Sopris RD, White River NF: in the Ruedi complex on Ruedi Reservoir, 15 mi up Frying Pan Road from Basalt at about 7,800 ft; sites look out over the reservoir. Not to be confused with Molly Brown near Leadville. --Claude FS, read 2026-10-28: 'Due to lack of water the campground is now closed for the 2026 season.' --Claude 2026-10-28

name: Coffee Pot Spring Campground
note: Small Forest Service campground on a south-facing aspen/spruce slope at about 10,100 ft, roughly 16 miles up Coffee Pot Road (FDR 600) from the Dotsero exit off I-70, a long, narrow one-lane gravel road. Not on the White River NF's campground list or its 2026 operating-dates sheet (checked 2026-10-28), and Campendium now lists it as dispersed camping; the loop still shows on imagery. Confirm with the Eagle-Holy Cross Ranger District before going. --Claude

name: Sunset Point Campground
note: 25 non-electric sites on a point in Lake Granby (Arapaho NRA), elev ~8,300 ft; max vehicle length 46 ft, sites 12-24 are the longer ones. Potable water but no threaded spigots, vault toilets, trash service, boat ramp; no hookups. First-come, first-served (not reservable on recreation.gov). --Claude

name: Swinging Bridge Campground
note: Browns Park National Wildlife Refuge (USFWS) on the Green River at the west end of the Wildlife Drive, beside the historic single-lane Swinging Bridge (20-ton limit, 8 ft 6 in at its narrowest). Reached by long gravel roads. --Claude The bridge fits a class-B or small class-C with the mirrors folded. --AWH 2026-10-28

name: Grant McCormick Memorial RV Park
note: Town of Holly municipal RV park on W. Highway 50, an overnight stop in far eastern CO. $20/night per the sweep (no rate on the town's pages as of 2026-10-28). Shade trees, picnic tables, enclosed play yard; tent spaces too. --Claude

name: Rifle Mountain Park
note: City of Rifle park, not the neighbouring Rifle Falls State Park, in a limestone canyon along East Rifle Creek, reached by a gravel road past the fish hatchery at the end of Highway 325, with over 250 bolted climbing routes. The 14 Huffman Gulch sites stay first come, first served; sites marked Van take no trailers. A 23-ft rig fits the larger drive-in sites. --Claude

name: Bassway Strip State Wildlife Management Area
note: Platte River WMA adjacent to I-80 SE of Kearney. Drive-in primitive camping: flat pull-offs along a gravel road, self-contained rigs fit, no facilities and no fires; no permit, FCFS, 3-night limit per 6 days. Riverside fishing access. Note: access bridge has weight limits (10-ton dual-axle / 23-ton trailer) — fine for a 23-ft Class C. Highway noise. --Claude

name: Big Alkali Lake State Wildlife Area
note: Nebraska Game & Parks WMA on Big Alkali Lake in the Sandhills, ~25 mi south of Valentine via US-83 and Spur 16B (well-maintained but narrow gravel). About 30 FCFS sites (no reservations); some have electric. Reviewers note leveled gravel big-rig-friendly sites to the right of the boat ramp plus a sandy dispersed area to the left. Vault toilets, picnic tables/grills, water spout/laundry house near entrance, boat ramp; no dump station. As a WMA this is drive-in vehicle camping (not walk-in/hunt-only). --Claude

name: Bridgeport State Recreation Area
note: NGPC state recreation area west of Bridgeport on five clear sandpit lakes (78 water acres) along the North Platte. 72 designated Basic camp sites plus ~130 non-designated primitive sites, all first-come first-served (no electric). RV dump/fill station near the entrance (open ~Apr 30-Oct 1); vault toilets, drinking water at the swim beach. Nebraska park entry permit required. --Claude

name: Calamus Reservoir SRA - Homestead Knolls Campground
note: Largest campground at Calamus Reservoir SRA, 6 mi NW of Burwell in the Sandhills: paved, level 50-amp back-in sites with mature shade; shower house, modern restrooms, water; dump station and laundry in the park. The white-sand swimming beach and boat ramp are a separate day-use area to the southwest. Some sites reservable up to 180 days out, the rest FCFS. Park entry permit required. --Claude

name: Dead Timber State Recreation Area
note: NGPC recreation area on a Logan Creek/Elkhorn oxbow off US 275, ~4 mi north of Scribner, beside Powder Horn WMA. 17 electric sites (30 A) in a loop at the south end of the oxbow; the four primitive sites have been closed by flood damage. First-come first-served, self-pay envelopes. Drinking water, primitive restrooms; no dump station. --Claude

name: Gallagher Canyon State Recreation Area
note: NGPC recreation area on Gallagher Canyon Reservoir, an irrigation lake whose level can drop in late summer, SE of Cozad (Dr. 752 off Rd 422). About 30 primitive sites without electricity on dirt tracks across the wooded peninsula west of the dam; first-come first-served year-round. Primitive restrooms; no drinking water, showers or dump station. --Claude

name: Victoria Springs State Recreation Area
note: NGPC recreation area at a wooded Sandhills spring oasis east of Anselmo. 21 electric sites plus about 60 basic non-pad sites; ten of the electric sites book online, the rest first-come first-served. Two housekeeping cabins; small spring-fed pond with fishing and paddleboat rentals. Nebraska park entry permit required. --Claude

name: Bancroft Municipal Park
note: Village of Bancroft municipal park on the village's SW/NW edge; ~5 drive-in electric+water sites (camping NW of the park off Public Rd) on open flat grass -- ample room for a 23-ft Class C. RV dump and flush toilets on site; no showers noted. Open May-Oct, roughly $6/night, very cheap. Not on recreation.gov -- book/inquire by phone via Ru-Des Mini Mart; effectively FCFS/call-ahead. RV Life unrated (0 star, price $). --Claude

name: Battle Creek Municipal Park
note: City-run 55-acre municipal park & arboretum (ball fields, pool, playground) on the south edge of Battle Creek. ~18 RV sites with electric (20/30/50 amp) and water; sanitary dump on site. FCFS, pay on site. No water feature at the park (Battle Creek/Elkhorn River not adjacent). Caveat (2026-11-05): the city's parks page doesn't mention camping and one trail guide lists only two campsites, so call City Hall (402-675-2165) before counting on a site. --Claude

name: Bloomfield City Park Campground
note: City of Bloomfield municipal park. 6 RV-only sites (no tents) with cement pads, full hookups (30-amp electric + water), fire pits, grills, picnic tables; flush toilets, swimming pool/playground in park. Open year-round. FCFS, pay at City Office or police drop box. RV Life unrated (0 stars). --Claude

name: Blue Valley Camping Area
note: City of Seward municipal campground at 730 S 6th St. 16 crushed-rock pads with 30-amp electric; pads fit large rigs (reviewer at 34 ft). Dump station, water hydrant, portable ADA restroom (no showers), playground. $15 senior 65+, $10 tent, FCFS via drop-box envelopes, open Apr 1-Nov 1, 7-day stay limit (48-hr interim). Sits in a city park west of the Big Blue River, not on the water. --Claude

name: Cody City Park
note: Village of Cody municipal park; small grassy camping area near the old grain elevator (shields US-20 noise), behind the C-store a block off the highway. Directory reports (Campendium, Allstays, a 2023 blog): ~4-10 unmarked full-hookup back-in sites (30/50 A, water, sewer) beside pedestals, dump station, max RV ~29 ft, restrooms not always open, $20 a night honor system (cash/check), FCFS, open ~May 1-Oct 15. The village has no website (the old villageofcody.com domain now forwards to an unrelated site); call the village clerk. --Claude
